outcome: No event since 26 January 2024 settles Nagata's conjecture on curves, any non-square case with r >= 10, or the value sqrt(r); the in-window items are conditional, reformulation, or Demailly-type lower-bound results, and one (Ha-Sivakumar, 17 Aug 2026) credits ChatGPT-5.6 Sol with the key idea of its proof.
problem_asks: (1) For every r >= 10 (the statement's threshold is r > 9), every set of r very general points p_1..p_r in the projective plane, and every choice of positive integer multiplicities m_1..m_r: any plane curve passing through each p_i with multiplicity at least m_i has degree d > (1/sqrt(r)) * (m_1 + ... + m_r). Equivalent forms in the sources: the multi-point Seshadri constant of O(1) at the points equals 1/sqrt(r), or the Waldschmidt constant of the points equals sqrt(r). (2) Read as a statement about the minimal degree: the conjecture says the minimal degree is at least (1/sqrt(r)) * sum of the m_i; the matching existence of curves of degree about m*sqrt(r) is classical (Nagata's upper bound, per search snippets) and is not the open part, which is the lower bound in (1). (3) Scope over r: all r >= 10. The perfect squares are settled (Nagata); every non-square r >= 10 is open according to every source I read. (4) For very general points, over the complex numbers in most sources and in characteristic 0 in the 2022 and 2026 sources. The statement does not restrict the multiplicities beyond positivity.

events.what_happened: Nagata, 'On the 14-th problem of Hilbert', Amer. J. Math. 81(3) (1959) 766-772. States the conjecture (in the Hilbert 14th problem context) and proves it when r is a perfect square; the same paper gives his counterexample to Hilbert's 14th problem. Dated to the year only. I did not open the 1959 paper; the citation and the 'perfect square, proved by Nagata' status come from the Wikipedia article I opened, and the square range (n >= 16) from the abstract of Ciliberto-Harbourne-Miranda-Roe (arXiv 1202.0475).
events.delivers: Proves the conjecture's inequality for r a perfect square (in the r >= 10 range: 16, 25, ...). Settles only the square cases; the abstract of arXiv 1202.0475 says 'Nagata's original result was the existence of a good ray for X_n with n >= 16 a square number'.
events.remains: Every non-square r >= 10 (all sources: 'remains open for every non-square r >= 10'), and the sharp constant for those r.
events.direction: Confirms the inequality for square numbers of points; cuts toward the conjecture in those cases only.

events.what_happened: Joaquim Roe, 'On the existence of plane curves with prescribed multiple points', arXiv math/9807066, v1 13 Jul 1998, v2 18 May 1999. For r general points and multiplicity m, proves d >= m(r-1) * prod_{i=2}^{r-1} (1 - i/(i^2+r-1)) and d > m(sqrt(r-1) - pi/8); the conjecture predicts d > m*sqrt(r). The abstract states no range of r for these bounds.
events.revisions: v1 13 Jul 1998; v2 18 May 1999 (changes not described on the abstract page).
events.delivers: A lower bound on the degree of a curve with multiplicity m at r general points: d > m(sqrt(r-1) - pi/8), plus a product-form bound. This moves the degree lower bound toward Nagata's m*sqrt(r) by an additive constant; it does not reach m*sqrt(r). It applies to arbitrary plane curves, not only irreducible ones (per a search snippet describing Roe's second bound).
events.remains: The sharp inequality d > m*sqrt(r) for all r >= 10 and all m.
events.direction: Partial lower bound in the direction the conjecture points, short of the conjectured constant.

events.what_happened: Ziv Ran, 'On the Nagata Problem', arXiv math/9809101, v1 submitted 18 Sep 1998. The abstract (as read through the fetch tool) says that Nagata's statement (N_r) is proved 'provided r = k^2 + alpha, 1 <= alpha <= 2k, k >= 3', with either alpha odd and alpha >= sqrt(2k), or alpha even and at least 6, and a condition on the fractional part of sqrt(r). The paper is then withdrawn: v2 (25 Apr 2011) and v3 (8 May 2013) carry the comment 'Withdrawn due to fatal error'. The error is not described in any source I could open.
events.revisions: v1 18 Sep 1998 (the claim); v2 25 Apr 2011 (withdrawn); v3 8 May 2013 (withdrawn; comment 'Withdrawn due to fatal error').
events.delivers: As claimed in v1 (and as the abstract words it): the inequality for non-square r in the stated families r = k^2 + alpha. Because the paper is withdrawn, this establishes nothing.
events.remains: Everything: the claimed families are not established, and no other case is claimed.
events.doubts: The author withdrew it for a 'fatal error' per the arXiv comment field. No source I opened describes the error, and my searches found no published comment on it.

withdrawn.what: Whole paper withdrawn; arXiv comment 'Withdrawn due to fatal error' on v2 (25 Apr 2011) and v3 (8 May 2013). The arXiv record does not name who withdrew it; 'author' is an inference.

events.direction: Would cut toward the conjecture (prove the inequality) for a family of non-square r; withdrawn, so no weight.

events.what_happened: Brian Harbourne, 'On Nagata's Conjecture', arXiv math/9909093, v1 16 Sep 1999 (only version). Modifying Roe's approach, gives an improved lower bound on the degree d of a plane curve through n general points with multiplicity at least m. The abstract says that in certain cases, for m not too large compared with n, the new bound implies the bound conjectured by Nagata. The journal version is J. Algebra 236(2) (2001) 692-702, per the Wikipedia reference list (not opened).
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv; journal J. Algebra 236(2) (2001) 692-702 per the Wikipedia reference list.
events.delivers: A sharper lower bound on d for general points; it reaches Nagata's bound only in a regime where m is small compared with n. The explicit formula is not on the abstract page.
events.remains: The conjectured bound for all n >= 10 and all m outside the regime stated in the abstract, and all non-square cases in general.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper, J. Algebra 236(2) (2001) 692-702 (per the Wikipedia reference list; the journal page was not opened)

events.direction: Lower-bound progress toward the conjectured inequality; reaches the conjectured value only in a restricted regime.

events.what_happened: Thomas Eckl, 'An asymptotic version of Dumnicki's algorithm for linear systems in CP^2', arXiv 0801.2926, v1 18 Jan 2008, v2 22 Jan 2008. Develops an asymptotic method for lower bounds of Seshadri constants of general points on P^2, and proves the lower bound 4/13 for 10 general points. No journal record found in my searches.
events.delivers: For 10 general points, a lower bound 4/13 (about 0.3077) for the Seshadri constant, as the abstract words it. Nagata's value for r = 10 in the Seshadri form is 1/sqrt(10) (about 0.3162). So this is a non-sharp lower bound on the Nagata quantity at r = 10, a non-square case.
events.remains: The gap between 4/13 and 1/sqrt(10) for r = 10, and every other r >= 10.
events.direction: Partial lower bound toward the conjectured value at r = 10; short of it.

events.what_happened: Ciro Ciliberto and Rick Miranda, 'Homogeneous interpolation on ten points', arXiv 0812.0032, v1 29 Nov 2008 (only version). The abstract says that for all (d, m) with d/m >= 174/55, the linear system of plane curves of degree d with ten general base points of multiplicity m has the expected dimension. Non-speciality statement; does not mention Nagata.
events.delivers: Expected dimension for ten general points when d/m >= 174/55 (about 3.1636, which is above sqrt(10), about 3.1623). This is the other side of the Nagata threshold: Nagata's inequality concerns d/m < sqrt(10), where existence is what is ruled out. So the result does not bear on the Nagata region.
events.remains: All d/m < 174/55 for ten points, including the Nagata region d/m < sqrt(10).
events.direction: Does not cut either way on the Nagata inequality; its region is disjoint from the one the inequality concerns.

events.what_happened: Ciliberto, Harbourne, Miranda, Roe, 'Variations on Nagata's Conjecture', arXiv 1202.0475, v1 2 Feb 2012 (only version). Abstract: using degenerations, examples of good rays (non-effective, hence nef, rays in the Mori cone) for the blow-up X_n at n >= 10 general points, for all n >= 10; and 'Nagata's conjecture for n <= 89 combined with a stronger conjecture for n = 10 implies Nagata's conjecture for n >= 90'. The venue (2013) is from a search snippet and was not verified.
events.delivers: Existence of good rays for all n >= 10 (cone structure, not the inequality itself). A conditional reduction: the conjecture for n >= 90 follows from the cases n <= 89 together with a stronger conjecture at n = 10. No new unconditional case of the inequality.
events.remains: The conjecture for every non-square n >= 10, the n <= 89 cases, and the stronger n = 10 conjecture the reduction needs.
events.direction: A conditional reduction toward the conjecture; no case of the inequality proved.

events.what_happened: Ivan Petrakiev, 'Homogeneous Interpolation and Some Continued Fractions', arXiv 1211.6380, submitted 27 Nov 2012 (only version). Abstract: 'if d/m < 2280/721, there is no curve of degree d passing through n = 10 general points' (multiplicity m), with similar results for other special n and a palindromic continued-fraction form of the bounds.
events.delivers: For r = 10 (a non-square case): no curve when d/m < 2280/721 = 3.16227461..., which is below sqrt(10) = 3.16227766... by about 3 x 10^-6. So nonexistence is proved for all d/m below 2280/721, a gap of about 3 x 10^-6 short of the Nagata threshold sqrt(10). The abstract does not say whether 2280/721 is sharp.
events.remains: The window [2280/721, sqrt(10)) for r = 10 (about 3 x 10^-6 wide), and every other non-square r >= 10.
events.direction: Near-sharp partial result for r = 10, from below the Nagata threshold; does not reach it.

events.what_happened: Dumnicki, Harbourne, Kuronya, Roe, Szemberg, 'Very general monomial valuations of P^2 and a Nagata type conjecture', arXiv 1312.5549, v1 19 Dec 2013, v2 5 Feb 2016. Uses valuations so that the number of points can be any real s >= 1. Argues that a Nagata-type statement should hold for real s >= 8 + 1/36, and computes Seshadri constants explicitly for s <= 7 + 1/9. Publication in 2017 is from a repository record surfaced by search and was not verified.
events.delivers: A Nagata-type statement for real numbers of points, via valuations: a conjecture for s >= 8 + 1/36 (which includes all integers s >= 9), and explicit Seshadri constants for s <= 7 + 1/9 (integers up to 7 only). This is an analogue (real-number and valuative), not the integer problem.
events.remains: The integer problem for r >= 10. A valuative or real-number conjecture is not a proof of it.
events.direction: Analogue; supports the conjectured pattern for real numbers of points; no new integer case.

events.what_happened: Karol Palka, 'The Coolidge-Nagata conjecture, part I', arXiv 1405.5917, v1 22 May 2014, v2 27 Aug 2014; Adv. Math. 267 (2014) 1-43. About the Coolidge-Nagata conjecture on rational cuspidal plane curves (Cremona equivalence to a line). Not Nagata's conjecture on very general points. Recorded because the names collide; discounted.
events.delivers: Partial results for the Coolidge-Nagata conjecture (for example, more than two singular points, or more than six maximal twigs). About a different question.
events.remains: The Coolidge-Nagata conjecture in general, and everything this record asks about.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published, Adv. Math. 267 (2014) 1-43 (journal reference in the arXiv record)

events.direction: Not about this problem; does not cut either way.

events.what_happened: Galindo, Monserrat, Moreno-Avila, Moyano-Fernandez, 'On the valuative Nagata conjecture', arXiv 2208.11041, v1 23 Aug 2022 (only arXiv version). Gives several equivalent conditions for a plane divisorial valuation to be minimal with respect to an ample divisor, using a valuative Seshadri constant; 'As a consequence, we derive several equivalent statements for the valuative Nagata conjecture and some related results.' Published in Research in the Mathematical Sciences 12 (2025), article 18, DOI 10.1007/s40687-025-00500-2.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv; journal version Research in the Mathematical Sciences 12 (2025), article 18.
events.delivers: Equivalent reformulations of the valuative Nagata conjecture (divisorial valuations, infinitely near points). Not a proof of that conjecture or of the classical statement. The abstract does not say whether any new case of the classical conjecture is proved.
events.remains: The valuative conjecture itself, and the classical conjecture entirely.
events.direction: Analogue reformulation; no direction for the classical problem.

events.what_happened: Michel Waldschmidt, seminar talk 'Two invariants related to two conjectures due to Nagata', Politecnico di Torino, 22 Sep 2022 (listing posted 23 Jan 2026). A survey of Nagata's conjectures and related invariants (Seshadri-type and Waldschmidt-type), recalling Bombieri's 1970 result. The abstract states no new theorem. Recorded as a discounted announcement.
events.delivers: Nothing new stated in the abstract; a survey of known invariants.
events.remains: Everything asked here.
events.direction: None; the talk does not cut either way.

events.what_happened: Ciliberto, Miranda, Roe, 'Quadric cones on the boundary of the Mori cone for very general blowups of the plane', arXiv 2310.10507, v1 16 Oct 2023 (only version listed). For the blow-up of the plane at s >= 13 very general points, constructs cones over 8-dimensional rational spheres on the boundary of the Mori cone. The abstract says this 'gives evidence for De Fernex's strong Delta-conjecture, which is known to imply Nagata's conjecture'. Journal acceptance (Collectanea Mathematica, 25 May 2024) is from a search snippet and was not verified.
events.revisions: v1 16 Oct 2023 on arXiv; journal acceptance 25 May 2024 per a search snippet.
events.delivers: Structure of the Mori cone boundary for s >= 13 very general points (non-effective, irrational rays). Gives indirect evidence for a stronger conjecture (strong Delta) that implies Nagata's. Does not prove the inequality.
events.remains: The inequality for every non-square r >= 10, and the strong Delta-conjecture itself.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted 25 May 2024 (per a search snippet; the journal page was not opened)

events.direction: Indirect evidence through a stronger conjecture; no direct cut on the inequality.

events.what_happened: Sankhaneel Bisui and Thai Thanh Nguyen, 'Lower bounds for Waldschmidt constants and Demailly's Conjecture for general and very general points', arXiv 2401.11297, v1 Sat 20 Jan 2024, v2 11 Apr 2025. Abstract: proves Demailly's conjecture (a lower bound for the Waldschmidt constant in terms of symbolic powers) for any set of generic or very general points in P^N, with results for sufficiently many general points and for general points in low dimensions. The arXiv comment gives Collect. Math. 77(2) (2026) 483-500. Dated six days before the frozen revision.
events.delivers: Lower bounds for Waldschmidt constants of very general points in P^N in Demailly's form, and for general points in some cases. The abstract does not say whether P^2 is among the 'low dimensions' covered. A Demailly-type lower bound is not the sqrt(r) value.
events.remains: The Nagata value sqrt(r) for very general r >= 10 points in P^2.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published, Collect. Math. 77(2) (2026) 483-500 (per the arXiv comment field; the journal page was not opened)

events.direction: Lower bound only; cuts toward a large Waldschmidt constant, not toward the sqrt(r) value.

events.what_happened: Cyril J. Jacob, 'Lower bounds for Seshadri constants on blow ups of P^2', arXiv 2404.11906, v1 18 Apr 2024, v2 7 May 2024, v3 12 Sep 2025 (comment: '12 pages, to appear in J. Algebra'). Abstract: lower bounds for Seshadri constants of ample line bundles on X_r (blow-up of P^2 at r points), unconditional for points on a curve of degree at most 3 and for r <= 8; for very general points, epsilon(X_r) >= 1/2 'if the Strong SHGH conjecture is true'. The abstract does not define epsilon(X_r).
events.revisions: v1 18 Apr 2024; v2 7 May 2024; v3 12 Sep 2025. A search snippet reports that v1 claimed a bound of 1 where v3 claims 1/2; I did not open v1 to check this.
events.delivers: Conditional on Strong SHGH: epsilon(X_r) >= 1/2 for very general points, with no restriction on r stated in the abstract. Unconditional bounds only for r <= 8 and for points on a cubic. The constant is not defined in the abstract. Inference (not verified in the body): it is not the multi-point constant of O(1) at r points, since a bound of 1/2 for all r would contradict the Nagata value 1/sqrt(r), which is below 1/2 for r >= 5. It is most likely a single-point Seshadri constant at a general point (a search snippet on the Ein-Lazarsfeld background suggests this).
events.remains: The Nagata inequality for r >= 10 (the multi-point constant). The abstract does not touch it.
events.doubts: The bound is conditional on Strong SHGH, which is open. The quantity is not defined on the abstract page. The arXiv comment says 'to appear in J. Algebra', an author statement and not a referee record. My searches found no public engagement with the paper.
events.direction: Conditional lower bound on a Seshadri constant that is probably not Nagata's; no bearing on the Nagata value as far as the abstract shows.

events.what_happened: Antonio Laface, Luca Ugaglia, Macarena Vilches, 'Equivalent conjectures on blowing-ups of P^2', arXiv 2405.07716, v1 Mon 13 May 2024, v2 26 Nov 2024. Abstract: SHGH for linear systems on the blow-up X_r^2 of P^2 at points in very general position 'is equivalent to the fact that each nef class is non-special'; a characterisation of asymptotic speciality via arithmetic genus of curves in D-perp; and 'if r < 2^n then any nef divisor of X_r^n is asymptotically non-special' for P^n. Journal record (J. Algebra 695 (2026) 432-445, DOI 10.1016/j.jalgebra.2026.02.010) is from a search snippet and was not opened.
events.revisions: v1 13 May 2024; v2 26 Nov 2024; journal J. Algebra 695 (2026) per publisher metadata (not opened).
events.delivers: A reformulation: SHGH on very general P^2 blow-ups is equivalent to every nef class being non-special. SHGH implies Nagata's conjecture per the sources, so this equates one stronger conjecture with another; it proves neither. The unconditional result covers P^n with r < 2^n, which for n = 2 means r < 4, outside the problem.
events.remains: The Nagata inequality for every r >= 10, and SHGH itself.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published J. Algebra 695 (2026) 432-445 (per publisher metadata surfaced by search; not opened)

events.direction: A reformulation; no direction on Nagata's inequality.

events.what_happened: Ciliberto, Miranda, Roe, 'Boundedness results for planar linear systems assuming the Segre-Harbourne-Gimigliano-Hirschowitz conjecture'. Hosted on Miranda's Colorado State University page with the file name 'CMRLinSysBoundedness10-04-2025' (the date is ambiguous: 10 April or 4 October 2025). No arXiv listing found. Per a search snippet (the PDF was not opened): conditional on SHGH, for fixed n >= 10 and genus g >= 2 there are finitely many complete linear systems on the blow-up of P^2 at n general points up to Cremona action, with a function g -> n(g) bounding the blow-ups needed.
events.delivers: Conditional on SHGH (which implies Nagata's conjecture): boundedness of linear systems of genus at least 2 on the blow-ups X_n for n >= 10. Nothing unconditional about the Nagata inequality.
events.remains: The Nagata inequality for every r >= 10, and SHGH itself.
events.direction: Conditional; no direct cut on the inequality.

events.what_happened: Tai Huy Ha and Aniketh Sivakumar, 'Polynomial interpolation and the Waldschmidt constant of points in projective space', arXiv 2608.16040, submitted 17 Aug 2026 (only version; math.AG with math.AC). Abstract: 'We establish Chudnovsky's Conjecture and, more generally, Demailly's Conjecture for any finite set of points in P^n_k, where k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0.' Abstract also: 'The key idea of passing to positive characteristic, as well as the broad plan of the proof, was suggested by ChatGPT-5.6 Sol.' and 'All mathematical arguments and proofs in this paper were developed, written, and verified by the authors.' The PDF body could not be extracted by the fetch tool, so the exact inequality and the P^2 case are unread.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: a lower bound on the Waldschmidt constant for any finite point set in P^n over characteristic 0 (Demailly's inequality, of which Chudnovsky's is the m = 1 case). Applied to very general points in P^2 it would be a lower bound on the Waldschmidt constant. The abstract states no explicit bound and does not mention sqrt(r). Background from search snippets, unverified: Chudnovsky-type lower bounds in P^2 give roughly (alpha+1)/2, about half the Nagata value for large r. Another snippet says Esnault and Viehweg (1983) already proved Demailly's conjecture for P^2, which would make the P^2 case not new.
events.remains: The Nagata equality, Waldschmidt constant of r >= 10 very general points in P^2 equal to sqrt(r). The lower bound in this paper does not reach sqrt(r) as far as the abstract shows. The matching upper bound is classical per search snippets.
events.doubts: No public verification found. The key estimate is stated for large characteristic p per a search snippet, so the characteristic-0 result passes through a large-characteristic argument. The follow-up by Pokora and Szemberg (arXiv 2609.16337) says its argument is based on the method 'used in this context by Hà and Sivakumar'; it does not say it verified their proof. The P^2 case may be older (Esnault-Viehweg 1983 per a snippet). The AI credit is in the abstract; whether the proof is correct is unverified.
events.direction: Lower-bound direction on the Waldschmidt constant; does not cut toward the sqrt(r) value either way.

systems.name: ChatGPT-5.6 Sol
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors' abstract, suggested the key idea of passing to positive characteristic and the broad plan of the proof. The abstract says all arguments and proofs were developed, written, and verified by the authors. The body was not readable, so the scope of the suggestion is unknown.
systems.basis_quote: The key idea of passing to positive characteristic, as well as the broad plan of the proof, was suggested by ChatGPT-5.6 Sol.

events.what_happened: Trung Hoa Dinh, 'Demailly's Conjecture in Quantum Language and Its Solution', arXiv 2609.05866, v1 5 Sep 2026, v2 9 Sep 2026. Abstract: an 'exact translation between fat-point interpolation in complex projective space' and a quantum language in which 'the Waldschmidt constant is the asymptotic particle cost per suppression order'; a finite-scale no-dark-state amplification theorem; 'Its asymptotic consequence is Demailly's conjectured inequality.' No Nagata mention on the abstract page. A search snippet says the full text cites Hà-Sivakumar and discloses use of GPT-5.6 Sol; the PDF was not opened, so that is unverified.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: Demailly's inequality for complex projective space, via a finite-scale theorem and an asymptotic consequence. The points and the bound are not stated on the abstract page. A Demailly-type lower bound, adjacent to the problem, not the Nagata value.
events.remains: Nagata's inequality for r >= 10 very general points in P^2.
events.doubts: Single-author preprint posted five weeks ago; no public engagement found. The argument is described only at abstract level in what I read.
events.direction: Lower-bound direction (Demailly-type); not the Nagata value.

events.what_happened: Shigeru Kuroda, 'Nagata's conjecture on a polynomial automorphism in positive characteristic', arXiv 2609.14611, v1 13 Sep 2026, v2 23 Sep 2026. About Nagata's 1972 conjecture that a particular automorphism of k[x1, x2, x3] is wild. The characteristic-0 case was proved earlier by Shestakov and Umirbaev; this preprint claims the case of characteristic k >= 7. Not the plane-curves conjecture. Recorded as a discounted namesake.
events.delivers: A different problem: a wild automorphism in positive characteristic >= 7 for Nagata's automorphism conjecture. Says nothing about very general points in P^2.
events.remains: Everything this record asks about.
events.direction: None for this problem.

events.what_happened: Piotr Pokora and Tomasz Szemberg, 'Demailly's Inequality for Finite Sets of Points in Positive Characteristic', arXiv 2609.16337, v1 14 Sep 2026. Abstract: 'We give a proof of Demailly's inequality in positive characteristic'. The argument uses 'the Frobenius-Hasse derivative method used in this context by Ha and Sivakumar', and a strict-growth lemma for initial degrees of symbolic powers of a finite set of affine points. Adjacent (Waldschmidt lower bound), not the Nagata value.
events.delivers: A positive-characteristic version of Demailly's inequality for finite point sets, per the abstract. The full argument was not read. Not the Nagata value.
events.remains: Nagata's inequality for r >= 10 very general points in P^2. Also the characteristic-0 result of Ha-Sivakumar is not independently settled by this paper.
events.doubts: The argument is built on the Ha-Sivakumar method, whose own characteristic-0 result is unreviewed. The abstract does not say that the authors verified Ha-Sivakumar's proof.
events.direction: Lower-bound direction; adjacent; not the Nagata value.

summary: Coverage: 39 web searches (listed verbatim under search.queries) and about 30 page fetches in six batches; primary arXiv abstract pages were read for almost every event, and the Wikipedia article was read through the fetch tool. The Nagata inequality for r >= 10 is open for every non-square r according to every source I read; the only settled cases are the perfect squares (Nagata, 1959). Nothing in the window (26 Jan 2024 onward) proves it, proves any non-square case, or moves the sqrt(r) value. Older partial results for r = 10 are Eckl (2008; lower bound 4/13 against 1/sqrt(10) = 0.3162 in Seshadri form), Ciliberto-Miranda (2008; expected dimension only for d/m >= 174/55, a region above sqrt(10)) and Petrakiev (2012; no curve for d/m < 2280/721, which is about 3 x 10^-6 below sqrt(10)); the last is the closest non-square result I found. Ran (1998) is the only claimed non-square proof, withdrawn in 2011 and 2013 for a 'fatal error' whose nature no source describes. In the window: (a) Jacob (18 Apr 2024) gives epsilon(X_r) >= 1/2 for very general points conditional on Strong SHGH; the abstract does not define epsilon(X_r), and by inference it is probably a single-point constant, not Nagata's multi-point one, because a bound of 1/2 on the multi-point constant would contradict the conjectured value 1/sqrt(r). (b) Laface-Ugaglia-Vilches (13 May 2024) show SHGH on very general blow-ups is equivalent to non-speciality of nef classes, a reformulation. (c) Ciliberto-Miranda-Roe (2025 preprint, date ambiguous) prove boundedness results assuming SHGH. (d) The Waldschmidt/Demailly line: Bisui-Nguyen (posted 20 Jan 2024, six days before the frozen revision) prove Demailly's lower bound for very general points in P^N; then Ha-Sivakumar (17 Aug 2026) state Chudnovsky's and Demailly's conjectures for any finite point set in P^n over characteristic 0, with the abstract saying 'The key idea of passing to positive characteristic, as well as the broad plan of the proof, was suggested by ChatGPT-5.6 Sol.' and that all arguments were developed, written and verified by the authors. The AI attribution is on a Demailly-type lower bound, not on the sqrt(r) equality, and the PDF body could not be extracted, so the exact inequality and whether the P^2 case is new are unread. A search snippet says Esnault and Viehweg (1983) already proved Demailly's conjecture for P^2; if so, the P^2 case is not new. Dinh (5 Sep 2026) and Pokora-Szemberg (14 Sep 2026) follow the same line; Pokora-Szemberg say their argument is based on the Ha-Sivakumar method. Two namesakes are recorded as discounted events: Kuroda (13 Sep 2026; Nagata's 1972 automorphism conjecture in characteristic >= 7) and Palka (2014; Coolidge-Nagata). AI search: nothing found on this conjecture. Searches for Claude, Fable, GPT, Gemini, AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, Lean and mathlib, DeepMind's formal-conjectures repository and Epoch's open-problem benchmark found nothing about it. The 2026 AI counterexample wave (Erdos unit distance, the Jacobian conjecture, Sra's GPT Pro counterexample survey, read to Appendix F) does not mention it. The record should be read with the Ha-Sivakumar attribution in mind: it is the only in-window event where an AI system is credited with load-bearing mathematics, and it concerns a neighbouring lower bound.
competing_reading: The strongest case that the window moved this problem: Ha-Sivakumar (with Dinh and Pokora-Szemberg) prove lower bounds on the Waldschmidt constant of any finite point set in P^n, which for very general points in P^2 is the very quantity Nagata's conjecture fixes at sqrt(r). A reader who counts any proved improvement to a lower bound on that quantity as a bound moved would record it as an in-window event for this problem, and then the AI credit for the key idea is load-bearing. Against that: the Chudnovsky/Demailly-type bound is weaker than sqrt(r) (about half of it for large r, by background knowledge I did not verify), the abstract makes no sqrt(r) claim, the P^2 case may be older (Esnault-Viehweg 1983, per a search snippet), and no human has checked the argument publicly. A second reading: Jacob's epsilon(X_r) >= 1/2 could be read as a Nagata-type statement if its constant is the multi-point one. I argue it cannot be, since such a bound would contradict the conjectured value 1/sqrt(r) for r >= 5; the abstract does not settle which constant it is.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The body of arXiv 2608.16040, which could not be extracted: the exact inequality it proves for points in P^2, whether it reaches sqrt(r) for any non-square r >= 10 (it would have to, to settle the problem), and whether Esnault-Viehweg or Chudnovsky already give the same P^2 bound. (2) The definition of epsilon(X_r) in arXiv 2404.11906 (the body of v3). (3) The date and arXiv identifier of the Ciliberto-Miranda-Roe 2025 preprint. (4) Public expert verification of 2608.16040, and of the Dinh and Pokora-Szemberg follow-ups. (5) Any proof of the sqrt(r) lower bound for a non-square r >= 10, with the author's own statement on AI involvement if any. (6) The Epoch FrontierMath Open Problems list and the DeepMind formal-conjectures repository, to check whether this problem is listed (not checked; both were only seen in search snippets).
